stories.headline: Grok 4.7 drops — same price as 4.6, stronger agent coding and self-checks
stories.why_read: Anand RTd day-1 takes all night; HN ~581; Next.js evals put it top-three for the first Grok.
body: SpaceXAI shipped Grok 4.7 on September 21 as a same-price, same-speed upgrade over 4.6 ($2/$6 per million under 200k prompts): larger base, longer RL on multi-hour tasks, tighter self-verification, native Grok Bot harness training, and a new safeguard stack. Launch scores put CursorBench 4.0 at 46.3% (xhigh) and EEBench at 64.0%, with day-one availability in Cursor, Grok Build, the Grok API, and a GitHub Copilot rollout.

Anand's overnight RTs tracked the human read: @kunchenguid's Firstmate day-1 (prompt-faithful, stable, conservative — ignore the loud public-bench hot takes), @theo noting Artificial Analysis task cost vs Astra, and @nextjs celebrating the first Grok in the Next.js evals top three. The story is not another leaderboard spike — it is whether agent harnesses actually feel different on Tuesday morning.

stories.headline: Cybercab #67 joins the Austin Robotaxi fleet — dedicated two-seaters hit 67
stories.why_read: Anand RTd @robotaxi's video; Texas DMV tally shows nine more Cybercabs and a 476-vehicle Austin fleet.
body: Tesla's purpose-built Cybercab count in Austin climbed again: @robotaxi posted Cybercab #67 joining the fleet overnight, and X News tallied nine new Cybercab registrations that push dedicated two-seaters to 67 alongside 409 Model Ys (476 autonomous vehicles total in Austin). Early paid robotaxi rides in the geofenced zone remain the live testbed while gold showroom units tour Sydney and China.

The timing matters with NHTSA's Special Order still on the clock for wheel-less Cybercab legality. Fleet growth plus Anand's RT of DHH's "What a time to be alive" clip keeps Austin's lounge-cabin robotaxi beat ahead of the regulatory paperwork — and ahead of Monday's China/Australia showroom thrills.

stories.headline: Nvidia DSX Ready: Tesla Megapacks qualified for AI factory power stacks
stories.why_read: Anand RTd Sawyer Merritt — Megapack is now on Nvidia's BESS shortlist for DSX AI factories.
body: Nvidia launched DSX Ready, a partner qualification for battery energy storage and cooling gear that matches its DSX AI factory reference designs. Tesla Megapacks are in the first BESS cohort — Nvidia's framing is blunt: power, cooling, water, and grid constraints now decide how much compute you can actually turn on.

@Tesla_Megapack amplified the same beat Anand RTd: Megapacks buffering data-center load and helping interconnection compliance. It is the physical-AI crossover — chips need watts as much as FLOPs — landing the same week Samsung/SK Hynix HBM shares ripped higher on memory demand.

stories.headline: U.S. Tesla new orders: Model 3 RWD and Model Y L Launch Series sold out for 2026
stories.why_read: Anand double-RTd Sawyer Merritt — Y L Launch now quoting Jan–Feb 2027; demand > supply.
body: Sawyer Merritt's inventory snapshot Anand amplified twice: Model 3 RWD and Model Y L Launch Series are sold out for new U.S. 2026 orders, with Model Y RWD/AWD nearly gone. New Y L Launch configs are already showing estimated delivery into January–February 2027.

Used Performance Y prices spiking and @bscholl's HW4/FSD "table stakes" quote RT'd by Anand rhyme with the same demand signal. Whatever the narrative on deliveries, the order book is telling a tighter story than Monday's China wait-time note alone.

stories.headline: Starship Flight 14 slips to NET Sep 28 — first orbital shot with 26 Starlink V3s
stories.why_read: Monday's ~Sep 22 pad window moved; trackers now hold Monday Sep 28 7:15am CT for B21/S41.
body: SpaceX's first true Starship orbital attempt is now No Earlier Than Monday, September 28, 2026 at 7:15am CT (12:15 UTC) from Starbase Pad 2 — a 75-minute window pending regulatory clearance. Booster 21 and Ship 41 still target ~275 km orbit, ~six orbits over ~10 hours, deployment of 26 Starlink V3 satellites (1 Tbps-class each), Gulf booster splashdown, and Pacific ship splashdown west of Chile.

Monday's edition had the pad-roll and an earlier ~Sep 22 framing; Tuesday's beat is the calendar slip plus the payload stakes. First operational Starlink on Starship remains the milestone even if the clock moved a week.

stories.headline: MiMo v2.6 — Xiaomi's open model tops HN; Pro price/perf analysis follows
stories.why_read: HN #1 at ~938 pts; Artificial Analysis already has a Pro intelligence/price card.
body: Xiaomi's MiMo v2.6 announcement led Hacker News (~938 points) with a companion Artificial Analysis write-up on MiMo-v2.6-Pro intelligence, performance, and price. It is another open-weight week entry after Qwen-Image-2.1 — labs outside the usual U.S. frontier set keep shipping runable models.
For Anand's shelf (LocalLLaMA taste, open LLMs, agent stacks), MiMo is the "can I actually try it" story next to Grok 4.7's closed API bump — open vs harness, both moving on the same Tuesday.

stories.headline: OpenAI + Anthropic + SpaceX paper value tops every U.S. tech IPO, 1980–2025
stories.why_read: Anand RTd Jason's chart — three private names vs 45 years of public tech debuts.
body: A Wall Street chart making the rounds (Jason Calacanis RTd it; Anand amplified) stacks OpenAI, Anthropic, and SpaceX private marks against the combined first-day value of every U.S. tech IPO from 1980–2025 — and the three private names win. X News framed the totals around multi-trillion private marks versus ~$4.1T of historical IPO day-one value.

It is a power-law postcard for Anand's IT/ET union: AI labs and launch companies concentrating value off-exchange while Flight 14 and Grok 4.7 ship in public. Treat the precise marks as chart-of-the-day, not audited books — the shape of the concentration is the news.

stories.headline: Attention is all you have — a sharp critique of the transformer monoculture
stories.why_read: HN ~844 pts; pairs with Visual Transformer Explainer still climbing the same front page.
body: alicegg.tech's "Attention is all you have" essay hit ~844 on HN, arguing the field's attention monoculture hard enough to sit next to the ever-green Transformer Explainer visualizer (~446). It is systems-taste reading: not another benchmark dump, but a provocation about what we stopped trying.
Tuesday's AI fold already has Grok 4.7 and MiMo shipping product; this is the counter-melody — why the architecture shelf got so thin — for readers who still care about the math under the agents.

stories.headline: Linear: AI coding made CI the bottleneck — so they reworked the pipeline
stories.why_read: HN ~256 — agent PRs outrun classic CI; the company rebuilt to keep up.
body: Linear's engineering post argues AI coding shifted the constraint from "write the change" to "wait for CI," then walks the redesign that lets agent-heavy PR volume keep moving. It is a practitioner note Anand's DevOps/DORA background will clock immediately.
Sits beside Plugin4Shell and Grok Bot agent fleets: when agents ship faster than gates, the gates become the product.

stories.headline: Cloudflare Python Workers hit general availability
stories.why_read: HN ~236 — Python joins JS/TS on the Workers edge runtime for real.
body: Cloudflare announced Python Workers generally available — Python workloads on the same edge Workers platform that already hosts JS/TS isolates. HN (~236) treated it as the missing language for edge glue and AI sidecar patterns.
For systems readers: fewer "ship a container for a 50-line handler" excuses, more cold-start and package-size craft at the rim of the network.

stories.headline: NASA's Mars Sample Return mission is dead
stories.why_read: Science.org + HN ~402 — flagship MSR canceled; Mars architecture reset.
body: Science magazine reports NASA's Mars Sample Return effort is effectively dead after cost and schedule blowouts, ending a flagship architecture that was supposed to bring Perseverance's cached cores home. HN (~402) framed it as a planetary-science gut punch next to private launch cadence.
Contrast with Starship Flight 14's Starlink-first orbital try: public Mars sample logistics stall while commercial heavy lift practices orbital ops with broadband birds.

stories.headline: Terry Tao: Advisory Group on Mathematics and Artificial Intelligence
stories.why_read: Fresh Tao blog post (~146 HN) — formalizing how math and AI should talk.
body: Terence Tao posted on the Advisory Group on Mathematics and Artificial Intelligence, continuing his streak of public calibration on where humans still matter in proof and discovery (Monday already carried his "why human mathematicians" note).
Pinned-taste fit: Physics/Chem/Math meeting AI without the hype layer — a committee with a blog trail beats another model card.

stories.headline: Tim Dettmers: Frontier AI on Your Own Hardware — open-source week notes
stories.why_read: HN ~167 — Dettmers on running frontier-class work locally; LocalLLaMA energy.
body: Tim Dettmers published "Frontier AI on Your Own Hardware" as part of an open-source week series — practical framing for serious local training/inference rather than toy demos. HN (~167) put it next to MiMo and open-weight chatter.
Reddit LocalLLaMA/MachineLearning hot.json returned challenge HTML this morning (blocked); Dettmers + MiMo + Laya/Kev cover the open/local shelf from HN and X instead.

stories.headline: Next.js evals: Grok 4.7 is the first Grok in the top three
stories.why_read: Anand RTd @nextjs — harness leaderboard signal beyond the launch blog.
body: Vercel's Next.js evals board shows Grok 4.7 as the first Grok model to crack the top three — a concrete harness result Anand RTd alongside the x.ai launch post. It complements CursorBench numbers with a framework-shaped coding eval developers already watch.
Useful counterweight to Artificial Analysis cost charts: capability on a known app scaffold, not only synthetic agent indices.

stories.headline: Lisa Su's AMD: from ~$2B market cap in 2014 to ~$1T
stories.why_read: Anand RTd Jon Erlichman's retrospective clip — the long arc of the AI GPU challenger.
body: Jon Erlichman's clip Anand RTd restates the Lisa Su era in one punchline: AMD roughly $2 billion when she became CEO in 2014, about $1 trillion today. It is anniversary-style finance content, but it maps onto the HBM/Nvidia-competitor narrative still driving Samsung and SK Hynix moves.
For the edition's chip beat: DSX Megapacks and HBM4 expansion are the near-term watts/memory story; Su's decade is the institutional memory.

stories.headline: HF #1: open multilingual System-1 decision model — Laya vs Jev wave continues
stories.why_read: Anand RTd Clement Delangue + Laya's builder thread; open classifiers still climbing.
body: Hugging Face's #1 trending model slot flipped to an open-source multilingual System-1 decision model days after TypeSafe Jev went viral — Clement Delangue's post Anand amplified. Laya's builder (@Nandakishorm1) is still in Anand's timeline and bookmarks explaining the Kerala-to-HF path and the 33ms decision-engine pitch.
Monday already carried Kev, Laya-on-M4, and Jev-as-Judge; Tuesday's update is the HF chart itself — open decision heads are a category now, not a one-off.

stories.headline: Bryan Cantrill: What Sun got wrong
stories.why_read: HN ~602 — Joyent/Oxide lens on Sun's missed futures; terminal-first comfort reading.
body: Bryan Cantrill's "What Sun got wrong" essay landed ~602 on HN — a systems-history autopsy from someone who lived adjacent to the wreckage and the surviving ideas. It is the kind of long-view systems writing Anand's Unix/IRIX taste still rewards.
No product launch, just institutional memory about platforms, culture, and timing — useful ballast on a Grok-and-Cybercab morning.

stories.headline: I don't want to read what you didn't write — AI prose fatigue
stories.why_read: HN ~740 — a practitioner essay against outsourcing your sentences to models.
body: Colin Breck's "I don't want to read what you didn't write" (~740 on HN) is the cultural twin of the agent boom: if models draft everything, readers start craving receipts of human attention. It is not anti-AI so much as anti-slop.
Paired with Linear's CI bottleneck and Grok 4.7 day-1 notes, Tuesday's meta-theme is trust — of code gates, of model behavior, and of the prose in between.

stories.headline: Apple documents how to turn off and restrict Apple Intelligence on Mac
stories.why_read: HN ~324 + companion essay (~276) — control surfaces finally showing up.
body: Apple's Mac Help docs for turning off and restricting Apple Intelligence features climbed HN (~324), with a same-day personal essay "I said no and Apple said yes" (~276) about consent and defaults. The pair reads as users reclaiming the off switch after a year of on-by-default AI chrome.
Useful systems note next to Monday's fm CLI story: Apple is shipping both the model surface and the admin knobs — enterprise-adjacent readers will care about the knobs.

stories.headline: JetBrains Air — a system of products for agentic software development
stories.why_read: Fresh JetBrains blog — IDE vendor packages an agent stack, not a single chat.
body: JetBrains introduced Air, framed as a system of products for agentic software development rather than a lone assistant pane. It is the incumbent-IDE answer to Cursor/Grok Build/Copilot cloud agents — packaging review, generation, and project context as a product line.
On a Grok 4.7 morning, every major tooling house is choosing a harness story; JetBrains just published theirs.

stories.headline: Transformers Explained Visually — Polo Club interactive still climbing
stories.why_read: HN ~446 — the visual explainer wave returns next to "Attention is all you have."
body: Georgia Tech Polo Club's Transformer Explainer interactive (~446 on HN) is back near the top of the front page beside the monoculture critique essay. It remains one of the cleanest ways to see attention heads, not just cite them.
Pedagogical ballast for a release-heavy Tuesday — especially useful if you are onboarding someone past the Grok 4.7 press release into the actual architecture.

stories.headline: Judge clears SpaceX land swap from Texas wildlife refuge near Starbase
stories.why_read: X News — injunction denied Sep 21; ~715 refuge acres for testing expansion path.
body: A South Texas federal judge denied a preliminary injunction on September 21, clearing SpaceX to proceed with a land exchange of roughly 715 acres from the Lower Rio Grande Valley National Wildlife Refuge for SpaceX acreage near the Massey Test Site. Environmental groups signaled they will keep litigating the broader case.
Infrastructure beat next to Flight 14: pad and test footprint politics move even when the launch NET slips a week.

stories.headline: NHTSA Special Order: Tesla must prove Cybercab legal to sell — under oath by Sep 29
stories.why_read: Holdover — deadline still ahead; sharper now that Austin Cybercab count hit 67.
body: NHTSA's Special Order still requires Tesla to answer, under oath, whether Cybercab can legally be sold without traditional controls — with the late-September response clock from Electrek's reporting still the live regulatory stake. Monday carried the order; Tuesday's fleet expansion makes the paperwork less abstract.
Keep this next to the #67 fleet lead: product is scaling in Austin while federal counsel drafts the sworn reply.

stories.headline: Samsung expected to more than double HBM4 / HBM4E DRAM output
stories.why_read: Holdover — still hot as Samsung/SK Hynix shares surge on AI memory demand.
body: Monday's Samsung HBM4/HBM4E capacity-doubling report remains the memory-supply spine under Nvidia DSX and AI factory buildouts. X News on Tuesday added the equity tape: Samsung and SK Hynix ripped higher on the same AI-DRAM thesis, with analysts still calling HBM tight into 2027.
Keep it while Megapack-for-DSX and Grok/agent demand keep arguing that watts and HBM, not just FLOPs, gate the boom.

stories.headline: Kev scales up — 0.6B/4B/8B Jev-like decision models on Qwen3
stories.why_read: Bookmark still hot — Jared Palmer's TypeSafe-compatible open decision family grew.
body: Jared Palmer's Kev update (bookmarked by Anand) ships 0.6B, 4B, and 8B Jev-like decision models on Qwen3 with LoRA + pointer-head technique, Apache-2.0 weights, and a TypeSafe-compatible API via base_url swap. Reported out-of-domain scores put Kev-8B near Jev with Mac-friendly latency claims on the 4B.
Together with Laya's HF chart climb, the System-1 open bench is no longer a single viral model — it is a small competitive field.

stories.headline: JPMorgan: Tesla robotaxi revenue ~$320B annually by 2035
stories.why_read: Holdover — still circulating; vertical-fleet thesis next to live Austin Cybercab growth.
body: JPMorgan's Rajat Gupta note projecting ~$320B annual Tesla robotaxi revenue by 2035 (mostly owned fleet, thin peer-to-peer share) is still on the X News carousel. Bulls call it conservative versus ARK-scale TAM slides; the capital intensity of owning the fleet is the quiet half of the pitch.
Read it against Cybercab #67 and the NHTSA clock: spreadsheet futures meet Texas DMV registrations.

stories.headline: Cybertruck: steer-by-wire OTA cut the turning circle by nearly two feet
stories.why_read: Holdover — @cybertruck + Wes Morrill still in Anand's bookmark stack.
body: Cybertruck's steer-by-wire / rear-steer stack still earns ink: an early post-SOP OTA shaved nearly two feet off the turning circle after Elon asked for more "magic," and @cybertruck's amplification remains in Anand's bookmarks. Long wheelbase, software-tightened curb-to-curb — the truck that improves geometry after delivery.
A clean software-defined-vehicle postcard while Cybercab's wheel-less design faces NHTSA questions of a different kind.

stories.headline: TFR over SpaceX McGregor — Roadster launch event still eyed for October 1
stories.why_read: Holdover — Joe Tegtmeyer TFR read still the best public breadcrumb for the reveal.
body: The Temporary Flight Restriction over SpaceX's McGregor site near Waco — cited by Joe Tegtmeyer as Roadster-launch-event choreography through early October — remains the cleanest public signal for a ~October 1 unveil. Low-altitude drone and aircraft limits in a 1.5-mile radius are not subtle.
Keep it on the board while Flight 14's NET slips: Starbase practices orbit; McGregor may practice theater.

stories.headline: Plugin4Shell: zero-click RCE across Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, Gemini CLI
stories.why_read: Holdover — agent-tooling RCE class still relevant as every IDE ships an agent stack.
body: Air Security's Plugin4Shell write-up on zero-click RCE patterns across Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, and Gemini CLI remains the security holdover while JetBrains Air and Grok 4.7 expand agent surface area. Tool plugins are the new supply chain.
If your CI is the bottleneck (Linear) and your agents write the PRs, this is why the trust boundary moved into the harness.

stories.headline: Halvar Flake: BlueHat Asia 2026 slides — an age of experimentation
stories.why_read: Anand RTd @halvarflake — first BlueHat talk since the Vista days, slides public.
body: Thomas Dullien (Halvar Flake) posted slides from his Microsoft BlueHat Asia 2026 talk — "An age of experimentation" — noting it as his first BlueHat since the Vista era. Anand RTd the PDF drop; it is rare primary-source security keynote material from someone who shaped binary analysis culture.
Worth the download next to Plugin4Shell: strategic security framing, not just another CVE thread.
